lens: Two fresh signings led a busy day: Thoma Bravo agreed a $4B+ take-private of insurance-tech platform Accelerant ($20.25/share; Morgan Stanley, Houlihan Lokey, Wells Fargo) and Dynatrace bought AI-observability firm Arize for $915M (JPMorgan) — on top of live Caesars, Payoneer and DoubleVerify proxies, even as the pure-play advisers kept sliding on an otherwise green tape.

stories.headline: Accelerant to be taken private by Thoma Bravo for $4B+ at $20.25/share; Morgan Stanley and Houlihan Lokey advise Accelerant, Wells Fargo advises Thoma Bravo
stories.why_it_matters: Accelerant Holdings (NYSE: ARX), the data-driven specialty-insurance risk-exchange platform, entered a definitive agreement to be acquired by Thoma Bravo in an all-cash take-private at $20.25/share — a 49% premium to the Aug 12 close and an enterprise value of more than $4B. Per the company's 8-K, Morgan Stanley is exclusive financial adviser to Accelerant's Board and Houlihan Lokey is financial adviser to the Special Committee (both sell-side); BMO Capital Markets and Wells Fargo advise Thoma Bravo (buy-side). Altamont Capital (Accelerant's largest holder, ~82% voting) and the founders intend to roll equity. A sponsor take-private of an insurance-tech platform runs committed-financing, multi-jurisdiction insurance-regulatory and shareholder-vote workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Morgan Stanley and Houlihan Lokey (Accelerant) and Wells Fargo (Thoma Bravo) — a $4B+ insurance-tech take-private runs committed-financing, insurance-regulatory and proxy diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: Accelerant agrees to $20.25/share take-private by Thoma Bravo ($4B+ EV)

stories.headline: Dynatrace to acquire AI-observability firm Arize for $915M; JPMorgan advises Dynatrace
stories.why_it_matters: Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) signed a definitive agreement to acquire Arize — an AI-observability company — in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $915M (~$815M cash plus replacement equity awards), expanding its AI-monitoring stack across the AI development lifecycle. The release names J.P. Morgan Securities as financial adviser to Dynatrace (buy-side); Qatalyst Partners advised Arize (sell-side). Expected to close later this quarter or early in Dynatrace's fiscal Q3, subject to regulatory review. An AI/software acquisition runs technology, IP and integration diligence workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage JPMorgan (Dynatrace) — an AI-observability acquisition runs technology, IP and integration diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: Dynatrace agrees to acquire Arize for $915M

stories.source: Dynatrace press release (Dynatrace to Acquire Arize)

stories.headline: Stocks rally to fresh highs but advisory names keep sliding — EVR -2.8%, JEF -2.3% on a green day
stories.why_it_matters: Equities jumped midday Aug 13 (S&P +1.26% to ~7,807, Nasdaq +1.89% to ~26,847, Dow +0.16%), with the VIX easing to ~14.6 and the 10Y down to ~4.63%. Most bank stocks joined the rally (MS +3.0%, JPM +2.2%, GS +1.7%, LAZ +1.3%) — but Evercore (-2.8%) and Jefferies (-2.3%) fell again, a third straight session of pure-play advisory weakness even as the tape ripped and fresh mandates piled up (Accelerant/Thoma Bravo $4B, Dynatrace/Arize $915M). The persistent divergence between advisory-stock softness and robust deal flow underscores that pipeline strength shows up in mandates before the tape.
stories.suggested_action: Lean on the deal flow, not the stock tape — three straight soft sessions for the pure-play advisers against a busy signing day is a cue to keep the conversation on live-process execution and room readiness.

Most bank stocks joined the rally (MS +3.0%, JPM +2.2%, GS +1.7%, LAZ +1.3%) — but the pure-play advisers kept falling: Evercore -2.8% and Jefferies -2.3%, a third straight session of advisory-name weakness even on a green day and a heavy signing slate (Accelerant/Thoma Bravo, Dynatrace/Arize). Values are live Aug 13 midday levels.

talking_point.quote: Third green session in a row for the tape — but the pure-play advisers, Evercore and Jefferies, fell again even as the market ripped. The mandates told the real story: Thoma Bravo's $4B take-private of Accelerant, Dynatrace's $915M buy of Arize, and fresh Caesars, Payoneer and DoubleVerify proxies, all with banks we cover. Pipeline strength shows up in signings before it shows up in the stock. Which of your live processes has the nearest diligence milestone this week?
